explanation: At noon on the June solstice, upright sticks cast no shadow in Syene, modern Aswan, but did in Alexandria. That angle and the distance between the cities gave him Earth's size.

claims.text: Around 240 BC, Eratosthenes estimated Earth's circumference by comparing the Sun's angle at noon in Syene and Alexandria.
Archimedes, Ptolemy and Pythagoras did not make this measurement.
At noon on the June solstice, upright objects in Syene cast no shadow, while in Alexandria they did.
Eratosthenes used the shadow angle at Alexandria and the distance between the two cities to calculate Earth's circumference.
Syene is the modern city of Aswan, in Egypt.
